business_problem: Decathlon's eight-year-old pricing system was struggling to scale and process millions of daily dynamic, marketplace, and local store prices.
solution_summary: Decathlon's eight-year-old pricing system was struggling to scale and process millions of daily dynamic, marketplace, and local store prices. Decathlon migrated to MongoDB Atlas, leveraging denormalized document structures and Online Archive to simplify data and reduce storage costs. One of these platforms is an internal pricing builder designed to centralize retail prices and maintain a single source of truth for global commerce. “The advantage of centralized pricing is that we can also centralize compliance with pricing laws, of which there are many, depending on the country,” explained Julien Lampin, Solutions Architect at Decathlon. These include local ‘subsidiarity’, which allows over 600 stores in France to adjust their own prices, as well as the launches of AI-driven dynamic pricing and a new third-party marketplace. As a result, the business’s daily data volume skyrocketed, reaching up to 1 million dynamic prices and 4 million marketplace prices.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas Online Archive
solution_components.role: Moves colder data out of the hot cluster while keeping it available for retention, analysis, and compliance.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Provides the managed document database backing Decathlon's modernized application platform.

data_flow: Operational data from legacy or distributed applications is consolidated in MongoDB Atlas Online Archive and MongoDB Atlas, where flexible document models support microservices, APIs, and downstream user experiences without batch-heavy synchronization. Upstream and downstream integrations include Kafka, AWS, APIs.
business_outcome: With MongoDB Atlas, Decathlon successfully migrated 100% of marketplace partners, eliminating relational bottlenecks to focus on business value.
